9_root_cause.banner: INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE: 29 games; every statistic below is descriptive, not a finding

classes.reading: P(play) is over-confident by 0.046 on average; Brier 0.0976. Participation errors enter unconditional stat error through (p - played) * mu; see decomposition.

classes.limitation: role proxy is derived from the forecast itself; confirmed-starter status is not in the outcome archive
classes.reading: Role = predicted-minutes bucket (a proxy: starter flags are not archived with outcomes). A starter-minus-bench bias gap away from 0 means the rotation shape (not the overall level) is wrong; bias is conditional on playing.
classes.statistic: minutes bias by role proxy (starter-like - bench)

classes.reading: verdict on the old simulator's systematic minutes under-prediction: INCUMBENT_UNDERPREDICTS_CONFIRMED; CHALLENGER_UNDERPREDICTION_NOT_DETECTED. Challenger bias +0.36 [-0.39, +1.02] min.
classes.statistic: minutes bias (pred - actual), challenger vs incumbent, paired

team_minutes_budget_error.note: sum over forecast players of P(play)*minutes minus actual minutes (240 + overtime is the true budget); only players with archived forecasts are summed

classes.reading: Per-minute rate (usage) accounts for ~81% of the squared-error budget (rate vs minutes components, points); a rate-component mean away from 0 is a usage / efficiency bias independent of minutes.
classes.statistic: error = r_pred*(m_pred - m_act) + m_act*(r_pred - r_act): rate component, points

classes.reading: If the opponent adjustment works this gap is ~0; a negative gap means the model under-projects against generous defences (adjustment too weak).
classes.statistic: points bias (pred - actual): generous-defence opponents minus stingy ones

pace.reason: game_forecasts carry no expected-pace context (not invented)

classes.reading: Game-total bias +4.79 [-4.23, +13.88]; per-game correlation between total error and mean player-points error: 0.866477283048264. A high correlation points at pace/environment (shared by all players) rather than player-specific rates.
classes.statistic: game total error (pred - actual) and correlation with mean player-points error

classes.reading: Largest departure of PIT variance from 1: threes (1.10; >1 = too narrow). Upper-tail excess > 0 means actual outcomes exceed the forecast 90th percentile more often than 10%.
classes.statistic: PIT variance ratio / tail excess (observed share beyond the 10%/90% quantiles minus 10%)

classes.reading: A negative gap means official reports sharpen P(play) as intended; ~0 means the report adds nothing measurable yet (e.g. opening week).
classes.statistic: participation Brier: official-report (REPORTED) minus unverified/projected information states

status_changes.note: status changes between pregame observations; forecasts generated before a change are the ones at risk

price_discovery.definition: share_h = sum(B_ref - B_h) / sum(B_ref - B_close), B = (mid - y_yes)^2 on contracts present at ref, h and close

classes.reading: Window with the smallest (best) model-minus-market gap: T-90. Prices converge toward the closing line; see price_discovery shares. A model edge that exists only at early windows and vanishes by T-10 is a timing signal, not yet value.
classes.statistic: model-minus-market Brier at each pregame window (negative = model better), plus market price discovery

classes.reading: Costs average 0.026 per contract; compare with the model's gross edge before reading any ROI. DNP legs and non-executable quotes are listed separately.
classes.statistic: per-contract trading costs (fee + slippage) and the gross-to-net P&L gap; DNP settlement effect
